Privacy Notice

Effective November 25, 2026 · Version 2.0 · Previous versions

What the Screen Gets

  • The items you approve
  • A link to each, which expires

What the Screen Never Gets

  • Your accountNever
  • Your other filesNever

bloop is a new, free side project run by one person in the UK. If you have an account, bloop stores your files in the EU until you delete them, and deletes a guest's file when the session ends. It never sells data and runs no ads, analytics scripts or trackers. The person who runs bloop can technically open stored files; the admin tools open one only after a report, and record it (who can see your data). How your files are protected is on the Security page. Write to hi@bloop.here about anything here.

This summary helps you read; the full text applies.

1 Who Is Responsible

Summary, not binding: In short: one named person runs bloop and answers for your data.

1.1 bloop is run by Duke DJ Saputra, an individual based in the United Kingdom ("bloop"), as a free side project in early access; it is not a commercial service. bloop is the controller of the personal data described here: it decides why and how that data is used.

1.2 Contact: hi@bloop.here. A postal address is available on request to that address.

1.3 bloop has no data protection officer; none is required. Write to hi@bloop.here.

1.4 Words used here: Account means a bloop account, opened from an invite. Library means the files stored in your Account. Screen means a browser showing bloop's page on a shared display, such as a room PC. Session means the time from Approve on your phone until it ends. Item means a file or link you approve for a Screen. Guest File means a file sent from a phone that is not signed in. Demo means the public sample at bloop.here, which uses bloop's own sample files.

2 What Works Today

Summary, not binding: In short: some of what is described here is not live yet, and each part says which.

2.1 bloop is in early access, and Accounts are by invite only. Rows below marked Planned describe data bloop will handle only once that feature is live. The current list of what is live is on the Security page.

2.2 bloop does not connect to Microsoft OneDrive or any other file service yet. Screens show files from your Library, Guest Files and bloop's sample files.

3 What bloop Collects

Summary, not binding: In short: your email, the files you store, and records of what you do with them.

3.1 The table lists each kind of personal data, where it comes from, and its status.

3.2 bloop stores the files you upload to your Library until you delete them (section 5). It does not look inside them except to check them and to make the copies it needs to show them, and it does not read your speaker notes for any other purpose: they are shown only on your phone, never on the Screen.

3.3 bloop does not use your data for automated decisions about you, and does not build profiles. Its checks refuse some files automatically, such as decks with macros; you can ask for a person to look at a refusal (section 9).

3.4 Photos sent as a Guest File are re-encoded on your phone before they leave it, which removes their location and other metadata. Videos have their location fields cleared on your phone. Files you upload to your Library are stored as you send them, with any metadata they carry; remove it first if you do not want it stored.

4.2 You have the right to object at any time to any use based on legitimate interests. Write to hi@bloop.here and bloop will stop unless it has compelling grounds that override your interests, or needs the data for a legal claim.

5 How Long bloop Keeps It

Summary, not binding: In short: your files stay until you delete them; a guest's file goes when the Session ends; records go on a fixed clock.

5.1 A daily job deletes data when its period ends. Data and Retention explains each period.

How long bloop keeps each kind of data

Your Account (email, passkeys, sign-ins) and everything in your LibraryKeptUntil you delete your Account, which takes effect 7 days after you ask (you can cancel by signing in before then); or, if you do not use your Account for 12 months, bloop emails you a warning and deletes it 30 days later unless you sign in
A Guest File's bytes and converted copiesKeptDeleted when its Session ends, and in any case within about 2 days: an hourly check, and a storage rule on the bucket, catch any the first step misses

Cloudflare's request logsKeptOff on the live site. If they are turned on, they record each request's details, including your IP address, and keep them at most 7 days

5.2 Restore history. bloop's database keeps a history that lets it be restored to any minute in the last 30 days, and the stores behind your Library list and live Screens keep the same. So a record bloop deletes, including one you asked bloop to erase, can still be recovered from that history for up to 30 days, and is then gone for good. bloop uses the history only to recover from a fault, and never to bring back data someone asked bloop to erase. Files themselves are not in that history: once a file is deleted for good, it cannot be recovered.

5.3 If bloop becomes aware of child sexual abuse content stored or sent through it, the law requires bloop to report it to the National Crime Agency. Once a report is sent, bloop must keep the reported content, the report, and related data it holds for 1 year from the report, and the report's reference for 5 years. bloop keeps nothing else for this reason, and deletes each item when its period ends.

5.4 When your Account is deleted, bloop deletes your email, passkeys, sign-ins, every file in your Library and its converted copies, and removes your email and file names from its Session records. It keeps only what 5.1 lists as kept for longer (reports, records of actions, an invite record for up to 90 days, and the block list), anything 5.3 requires, and sends one email to say it is done.

6 Who Can See Your Data

Summary, not binding: In short: you, the Screens you choose, and the one person who runs bloop when there is a reason.

6.1 You see your Library, your sign-ins and your live Screens on your phone or computer. A Screen gets only the Items you approve for it, and only for the Session. Your speaker notes go only to your phone.

6.2 The person who runs bloop. Your files are encrypted at rest by Cloudflare, but they are not end-to-end encrypted: bloop's server must read them to convert and show them. So the person who runs bloop can technically open any file or record bloop stores, using bloop's admin tools or the Cloudflare account that hosts it. bloop's admin tools show Accounts, invites, reports and records of actions, and the names, types and sizes of files; they open a file's contents only when that file has been reported. bloop looks at a file's contents only to act on a report about it, to fix a fault you ask it to look at, or when the law requires it, and never for a report of child sexual abuse content, which goes to the National Crime Agency unopened. Every action through bloop's admin tools is recorded with its reason, each opened file included. The Cloudflare account is protected by multi-factor sign-in.

6.3 No one else at bloop can see your data: bloop has no other staff.

8 Where Data Is Stored

Summary, not binding: In short: stored in the EU, run by a US company, with legal safeguards.

8.1 bloop's database, your Library and Guest Files are stored in the EU, and files are converted in the EU. bloop never claims "UK only": Cloudflare is a US company, and a request is handled at the Cloudflare data center nearest the person making it. This is the complete list of what may be stored outside the EU:

  1. (a) bloop's own logs and error reports (Workers Logs and Workers Issues): lines in a fixed shape with no IP address and no URL, which can include the internal ID of a Screen or of your Library (5.1);
  2. (b) usage counts (Workers Analytics Engine), which hold no IDs, names or file names;
  3. (c) the converter's program image, which holds code and never user data;
  4. (d) what Tally, Apple and Anthropic handle, as section 7 describes.

8.2 Where data goes outside the UK, the safeguards are the UK's adequacy regulations for the EU, and for the US the UK-US data bridge: Cloudflare is certified to the UK Extension of the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. Cloudflare's data processing terms add the EU Standard Contractual Clauses with the UK Addendum in case that certification lapses. Tally's, Apple's and Anthropic's transfers follow their own published terms.

10 Your Rights

Summary, not binding: In short: see, fix, move or delete your data, much of it yourself; bloop answers within a month.

10.1 You have the right to:

  1. (a) get a copy of your data (access);
  2. (b) have it corrected;
  3. (c) have it erased;
  4. (d) restrict how it is used;
  5. (e) receive it in a portable format;
  6. (f) object, as in 4.2;
  7. (g) ask a person to look again at a file bloop's checks refused;
  8. (h) withdraw consent to the waitlist at any time, without affecting what came before.

10.2 Much of this you can do yourself, in Account: Export downloads your original files and a data file of your Account, sign-ins, Sessions and records; Delete Account erases everything as 5.4 describes; and you can delete any file, rename it, or change your email.

10.3 For anything else, write to hi@bloop.here. bloop replies within one month, and may ask you to prove who you are first. In some cases the law allows a longer time or a refusal; bloop will say why.

10.4 Once OneDrive is connected, tap Disconnect OneDrive on any phone while you approve: bloop deletes its stored access and every sign-in ends at once, a lost phone's included. You may also be able to remove bloop in My Apps (myapplications.microsoft.com); your IT team can remove it for everyone in Microsoft Entra.

11 How to Complain

Summary, not binding: In short: tell bloop first; you can always go to the ICO.

11.1 To complain about how bloop uses your data, write to hi@bloop.here with "Complaint" in the subject. bloop acknowledges a complaint within 30 days, looks into it without undue delay, and tells you the outcome.

11.2 You may also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), the UK regulator, at any time, at ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint, which lists its helpline and postal address. The ICO usually expects you to raise it with bloop first.

12 Children

Summary, not binding: In short: Accounts are for adults; bloop is not made for children.

12.1 Accounts are for adults (18 or over) at universities, colleges and workplaces, by invite only. bloop is not made for children, and does not knowingly hold an Account for anyone under 18; if it learns of one, it deletes it. A Guest File, from anyone, is deleted when its Session ends, except as 5.3 describes.

13 Changes to This Notice

Summary, not binding: In short: every change is dated here, and big ones are announced first.

13.1 bloop will post any change here with a new version and date. For a material change, bloop will say so on this page and email Account holders and people on the waitlist before it takes effect.

What Changed
